newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's Roh and Chun drop appeals.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's Roh and Chun drop appeals.

text.p: Disgraced former South Korean presidents Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan will not launch final appeals against their convictions for mutiny, treason and bribery, their lawyers said on Monday.
A Seoul appeals court last Monday commuted Chun's death sentence to life in jail and cut Roh's prison term to 17 years from 22-1/2 years.
Monday was the deadline to challenge the sentences in the Supreme Court, South Korea's final court of appeal.

The convictions relate to a 1979 coup, an army massacre that crushed democratic resistance in 1980 in the southern city of Kwangju and slush funds of hundreds of millions of dollars the one-time heads of state amassed while in office.
"We won't appeal. President Roh doesn't want to cause any more worries to the public over this incident," Roh's lawyer Han Young-suk said by telephone.

Chun's lawyer, Lee Yang-woo, said: "President Chun doesn't want to disgrace the country with the troubles of history when it faces difficulties at home and abroad. It won't help the country's interests to continue the trial."
Han said the only reason Roh made an initial appeal was because Chun wanted to challenge his death sentence.
Chun and Roh are lifelong friends, and at their trial comforted each other by briefly squeezing hands as they stood side-by-side in the dock along with former aides and military subordinates.
Chun was president from 1980-88 and Roh succeeded him until 1993, when current President Kim Young-sam took office.
The decisions on Monday appeared likely to end Chun and Roh's involvement in the so-called "trial of the century" that has gripped South Korea.
Before the comments by lawyers for Chun and Roh, a state prosecutor said the prosecution was undecided on whether to pursue Chun and Roh any further. Prosecutors are seeking heavier punishment.
"We could drop the appeal if Chun and Roh drop theirs," prosecutor Lim Sung-duk had said.
However, he said prosecutors planned appeals over former generals charged with Chun and Roh for mutiny and sedition.

Thirteen one-time generals were convicted and one was acquitted. State prosecutors will appeal against the acquittal ruling as well as the jail sentences imposed on nine of the former officers, dropping cases against the other four.

Nine businessmen were convicted of bribing Roh, and five appealed to the lower court, which suspended all of their jail sentences. Of the five, Daewoo Group chairman Kim Woo-choong and the chairman of the Dong Ah Group, Choi Won-su, have announced appeals to the Supreme Court.
Kim's two-year jail sentence was suspended for three years while Choi's 2-1/2 year prison term was suspended for four years.
"The sentence is not a problem. What matters is that a conviction will bring various restrictions on the chairman's activities," said a Daewoo legal counsellor.
The Supreme Court deliberates on the legal basis of criminal convictions and can alter any sentences heavier than 10 years in jail, a prosecution official said.
